title: Polynomial dualizing objects for flat ring epimorphisms
statement:
Let $R\to A$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings, flat as in [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], such that multiplication $A\otimes_R A\to A$ is an isomorphism of rings. Let $P=R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\twoheadrightarrow A$, $n\geq0$, be a polynomial presentation [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], and suppose $A[0]$ is perfect over $P$, meaning it is isomorphic to a bounded complex of finitely generated projective $P$-modules [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex]. In ordinary module derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], write $C_B^T$ for the derived coinduction of [def-trf-derived-coinduction]. Put $P_A=P\otimes_R A=A[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$, let $a_i$ be the image of $x_i$ in $A$, and give $A$ the $P_A$-algebra structure by $x_i\mapsto a_i$. There are isomorphisms in $D(A)$
$$C_A^{P_A}(P_A)\cong A[-n],\qquad C_A^P(P)[n]\cong A[0].$$
The first identification on top cohomology is the dual Koszul identification [def-sc-koszul-dual-complex] for the ordered sequence $x_1-a_1,\ldots,x_n-a_n$, with its conormal basis in that order. The second identification is $A$-linear for the original coinduction action. The assertions include $A=0$ and $n=0$ and require no Noetherian or regular-base hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 0C0H (lemma-upper-shriek-localize), self-base-change calculation, expanded using the perfect polynomial model and the ordered graph Koszul complex; the hypotheses are stated algebraically as flatness, multiplication being an isomorphism, and polynomial perfectness.

proof.text: Put $S=P_A=A[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ and $t_i=x_i-a_i$. Successively substituting $x_j=a_j$ gives $S/(t_1,\ldots,t_i)=A[x_{i+1},\ldots,x_n]$: the inverse sends a remaining variable to its class, and the two composites fix every coefficient and variable. Thus $S/(t_1,\ldots,t_n)=A$. Multiplication by $t_i$ on the preceding quotient is injective: regard a nonzero polynomial as a polynomial in $x_i$; its highest nonzero coefficient remains the coefficient of the next power after multiplication by the monic polynomial $x_i-a_i$. This proves precisely the successive injectivity hypothesis, without requiring a proper ideal or a nonzero coefficient ring.

source.place: Tag 0C0H (lemma-upper-shriek-localize), self-base-change graph calculation expanded by polynomial substitution.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-regular-sequence-koszul-regular] to $S$, $M=S$ and the ordered list $t_1,\ldots,t_n$, using the injectivity just proved. Its Koszul complex $K$ resolves $A$. By [lem-sc-koszul-conormal-basis] the classes of these $t_i$ give the ordered $A$-basis of $I/I^2$, where $I=(t_1,\ldots,t_n)$. Apply [lem-sc-koszul-regular-sequence-dual-complex] over $S$: $\operatorname{Hom}_S^\bullet(K,S)$ has cohomology only in degree $n$, equal to $\bigwedge_A^n\operatorname{Hom}_A(I/I^2,A)$. Evaluation on the ordered conormal basis identifies this determinant with $A$, sending the wedge of the dual basis to $1$. This is the ordered dual Koszul identification, with the differential convention of [def-sc-koszul-dual-complex].

source.place: Tag 0BQZ (lemma-regular-immersion-ext), local dual Koszul calculation; More on Algebra Tags 062F, 062I and 0CEM.

proof.text: Write $E=C_A^S(S)$. Its scalar restriction is $R\operatorname{Hom}_S(A,S)$ by [lem-trf-derived-coinduction-adjunction]. The bounded finite-free resolution $K\to A[0]$ computes this derived Hom by [lem-sc-derived-hom-projective-resolution]. Consequently the preceding calculation gives $H^i(E)=0$ for $i\ne n$ and $H^n(E)\cong A$. This last identification is $A$-linear for the coinduction action: if $b\in A$ and $s\in S$ lifts $b$, then on $\operatorname{Hom}_S(A,J)$ for a K-injective $J$ one has $(b h)(a)=h(ab)=h(sa)=s h(a)$. Thus precomposition acts on cohomology by the same scalar as the Koszul calculation. Apply [lem-sf-derived-concentrated-single] in the abelian category of $A$-modules and use this top-cohomology identification to obtain $E\cong A[-n]$ in $D(A)$, with the specified normalization.

source.place: Tags 0A70 (lemma-right-adjoint), 0A71 (lemma-RHom-ext), together with Tag 0BQZ and Derived Categories Tag 08J5 (remark-truncation-distinguished-triangle).

proof.text: Flatness of $A/R$ and [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact] imply that termwise tensor with $A$ preserves acyclic complexes and quasi-isomorphisms: tensor the exact cycle-boundary sequences. Hence ordinary tensor with $A$ computes derived tensor, by applying it to any resolving quasi-isomorphism. The same applies to $S/P$, since $N\otimes_P S=N\otimes_R A$ for every $P$-module $N$. Multiplication identifies $A\otimes_P S=A\otimes_R A$ with $A$; under this identification $x_i$ acts by $a_i$. For every complex $V$ of $A$-modules, the map $V\to V\otimes_R A$, $v\mapsto v\otimes1$, is an isomorphism: use $V\otimes_R A=V\otimes_A(A\otimes_R A)$ and the assumed multiplication isomorphism. On pure tensors the associativity map sends $v\otimes(a\otimes b)$ to $av\otimes b$, and multiplication gives its inverse identification with $V$. In particular $v\otimes b=bv\otimes1$. These maps commute with differentials.

Put $D=C_A^P(P)$ and $U D=R\operatorname{Hom}_P(A,P)$, using [lem-trf-derived-coinduction-adjunction]. Apply [lem-pc-base-change-rhom-perfect] to $P\to S$, the perfect $P$-object $A[0]$ of the hypothesis, and $P[0]$. This gives an isomorphism in $D(S)$
$$ (U D)\otimes_P^{\mathbf L}S\ \cong\ R\operatorname{Hom}_S(A\otimes_P^{\mathbf L}S,S). $$
Step 4 identifies its right side with $R\operatorname{Hom}_S(A,S)$ and identifies its left side, after restriction to $P$, with $U D$: on a representative of $D$ by $A$-modules the latter identification is $v\mapsto v\otimes1$, with inverse multiplication. Thus there is a $P$-linear cohomology isomorphism $H^i(D)\cong H^i(E)$ for every $i$. This application uses perfectness exactly as stated, and no Noetherian hypothesis; flatness justifies both ordinary base-change identifications.

source.place: Tag 0A6A (lemma-base-change-RHom), clause (1), with Equation 0E1X and the flat self-base-change of Tag 0C0H.

proof.text: For $b\in A$ choose a lift $p\in P$ along the given surjection. On $\operatorname{Hom}_P(A,J)$ its original coinduction action equals multiplication by $p$, since $h(ab)=h(pa)=p h(a)$. On $\operatorname{Hom}_S(A,J')$ it likewise equals multiplication by the image of $p$ in $S$; this image evaluates to $b$. Consequently the $P$-linear cohomology comparison of step 5 is $A$-linear for these original actions: apply $P$-linearity to a lift of each $b$. From step 3 it follows that $H^i(D)=0$ for $i\ne n$ and $H^n(D)\cong A$ as $A$-modules. Now [lem-sf-derived-concentrated-single], applied in $D(A)$, gives $D\cong A[-n]$ and hence $D[n]\cong A[0]$. This establishes an isomorphism in $D(A)$ without assuming that an isomorphism after restriction lifts there. For $n=0$ the Koszul complex and its dual each have the single term $A$, and the empty determinant basis gives $1$; all steps still apply. If $A=0$, both coinduced complexes are zero by [def-trf-derived-coinduction], so both assertions hold in the zero category $D(0)$.
